note: Round 1 taxonomy. Records are web-search titles only (source websearch), so pains are read from thread and question titles on BiggerPockets, Wall Street Oasis and Quora. A pain is a problem in the room's words, not a topic.

pains.label: CoStar (and paid LoopNet or Crexi) costs too much for a small shop; is it worth it, and what is the cheap alternative?
pains.definition: Members ask what CoStar costs, whether CoStar, a paid LoopNet membership or Crexi Intelligence is worth the money, and what the free or affordable alternative is. Includes subscription and contract complaints.

pains.label: Is a warehouse a good buy at all, and what income or return can I expect?
pains.definition: First-timers ask whether warehouses, flex or small-bay industrial are worth buying, the pros and cons, where to start, and how much a building will earn.

pains.label: Is this deal any good? I have no one to check my numbers and terms
pains.definition: A member has a specific deal (NNN lease, ground lease, cap rate, NOI, small-town income) and wants help judging the numbers and lease terms before buying.

pains.label: I can't underwrite an industrial deal properly; is a paid modelling course worth it?
pains.definition: How to learn or speed up underwriting and financial modelling for industrial and development deals, and whether courses like the A.CRE Accelerator are worth the money. Firms also hire analysts for this.

pains.label: Finding warehouse deals, especially off-market, before everyone else
pains.definition: Where and how to source deals that are not on LoopNet: off-market properties, cold calling, owner lists.

pains.label: What to check before I buy, and what the Phase 1 environmental, appraisal and inspections cost
pains.definition: Due diligence at purchase: Phase 1 environmental site assessment, appraisal, red flags, what to look for, and what those third-party reports cost.

pains.label: Getting the loan: pre-approval hurdles, down payment, which lender, structure with partners, a mortgage I can't afford
pains.definition: Commercial loans for warehouses: pre-approval obstacles, lenders for NNN property, private vs hard money, SBA 504, down payments, loan structure with partners, refinancing at maturity and broker fees. Includes not being able to pay the mortgage.

pains.label: Raising money from friends, family and small investors for a first deal, and how to structure the terms
pains.definition: How to find investors and raise equity for a first deal or syndication, how to structure syndication or joint-venture terms, and the steps to set one up.

pains.label: Raising other people's money without breaking securities rules: co-GP, finder's fees, broker licence, Reg D
pains.definition: Members ask how to raise capital for their own or someone else's syndication legally: co-GP and fund-of-funds structures, whether fees need a broker licence, SEC exemptions, accredited-investor rules, Form D and state blue-sky filings.

pains.label: The PPM, operating agreement and syndication attorney cost too much, and when do I need them?
pains.definition: Start-up legal costs of a syndication: private placement memorandum, operating agreement, term sheet, attorney fees, buying a PPM template, and at what point in the deal to get the documents.

pains.label: Tracking investor commitments, distributions and updates once outside investors are in; which software?
pains.definition: Syndicators ask how to track investor commitments, send updates, manage distributions and investor relations, and which syndication or investor-portal software to use.

pains.label: Syndications fail and people lose everything: fear of a bad deal or a bad sponsor
pains.definition: Stories and fears of syndications failing, sponsors behaving badly, investors losing money, and how an LP or new GP protects themselves.

pains.label: Is a cost segregation study worth the fee on my building?
pains.definition: Owners ask when a cost segregation study makes sense, at what price point it pays off, and whether it is worth it for a smaller property.

pains.label: 1031 exchange: the 45 and 180 day clock, what qualifies, and what if it fails
pains.definition: Questions about 1031 exchange deadlines, nominating replacement property, exchanging residential into commercial, partial exchanges and failed exchanges.

pains.label: Finding tenants for an empty warehouse or godown, and dealing with a tenant who defaults
pains.definition: Owners ask where to find tenants, how to rent a warehouse at a good rate, and what to do when a tenant defaults on the lease.

pains.label: Running an NNN lease: what management fee and CAM is fair and who pays it
pains.definition: Questions about property management fees on industrial and NNN buildings, whether management fees can be included in NNN charges, CAM charges, and running a flex space on triple-net leases.

pains.label: Building or converting flex and warehouse space: is it still viable, what does it cost, contractors don't call back
pains.definition: Members ask whether flex-space development still pencils, what construction choices cost, how to convert a warehouse to flex, what to do after buying a warehouse to rehab, and complain about contractors not returning calls.
